extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents, and patent practitioners in India
extracted.subtask_description: Explanatory guidance on the Indian Patents Act and Rules covering government acquisition, conditions of grant, patent agents' registration and conduct, patent rights and co-ownership, term/renewal, patents of addition, and restoration of lapsed patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition of inventions and patents by the Central Government (Section 102)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Central Government may, if satisfied that it is necessary that an invention which is the subject of an application for a patent or a patent should be acquired from the applicant or the patentee for a public purpose, publish a notification to that effect in the Official Gazette, and thereupon the invention or patent and all rights in respect of the invention or patent shall... stand transferred to and be vested in the Central Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of the acquisition shall be given to the applicant and, where a patent has been granted, to the patentee and other persons appearing in the register as having an interest. The Central Government shall pay to the applicant/patentee such compensation as may be agreed; if no agreement, compensation may be determined by the High Court on reference (considering expenditure incurred, term, manner and period of working including profits, and other relevant factors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant of patents to be subject to certain conditions (Section 47)
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant of a patent under this Act shall be subject to the condition that certain uses by or for the Government or persons shall not be excluded by the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically includes: (1) Government may make/import patented machines/articles for its own use; (2) Government may use patented processes for its own use; (3) Any person may use patented machines/processes for experiment or research including instruction to pupils; (4) For medicines/drugs, Government may import for its own use or for distribution in specified medical institutions by notification in the Official Gazette. Also noted: Government can act if medicine cost is prohibitively high.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bolar provision and parallel imports (Section 107A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any act of making, constructing, using, selling or importing a patented invention solely for uses reasonably related to the development and submission of information required under any law regulating the product shall not be considered infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 107A(a) protects regulatory-testing activities; Section 107A(b) provides that importation of patented products by any person from a person duly authorised to produce/sell/distribute the product shall not be infringement — enabling parallel import rights to stabilize price in India.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register of patent agents (Section 125 and Rule 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Controller maintains a register called the 'register of patent agents' containing names, addresses and other particulars of persons qualified for entry under section 126.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register maintained at Head Office (Calcutta) will contain name, nationality, principal place of business, branch office address, qualifications and date of registration and other prescribed particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications for registration as patent agents (Section 126)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person will be qualified for entry in the register if he/she fulfils specified conditions: citizenship, age, qualifications and payment of fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (a) citizen of India; (b) at least 21 years old; (c) degree in Science, Engineering or Technology from an Indian university or equivalent specified by Central Government, and in addition either (i) [text indicates alternatives] OR (ii) has passed the qualifying examination OR (iii) has for at least ten years functioned as an examiner or discharged functions of the Controller under section 73 (but ceased to hold such capacity at application time); (d) paid prescribed fee. Persons registered before the 2002 amendment remain entitled on re-registration with fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying examinations for patent agents (Rule 110)
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifying examination consists of a written test and a viva-voce; written test is two papers of 100 marks each: (1) Patents Act and Rules; (2) Drafting and interpretation of Patent specification and other documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualifying marks: 50% each for written paper and viva voce; a candidate passes only if he obtains an aggregate of 60% of the qualifying marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration procedure after passing examination (Rule 111)
rubrics_metrics.description: After a candidate passes the qualifying examination and after obtaining any further information the Controller considers necessary, and on receipt of the fee, the Controller will enter the candidate's name in the register and issue a certificate of registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller may require additional information before entry; certificate issued on registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Details required in application for registration (Rule 112 / Form 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant entitled to registration shall make request on Form 22 with prescribed fee giving information regarding practice as patent agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details to be entered: (a) Name and Qualification; (b) Address of office including branch office; (c) Date of payment of prescribed fee; (d) Other details as may be necessary. Fee example given: Rs.2000/-.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualification for registration as a Patent Agent (Rule 114)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person will not be eligible to be registered as a patent agent if specified disqualifying conditions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disqualifying conditions include: adjudged of unsound mind; an undischarged insolvent; (exceptions for discharged insolvent with court certificate); convicted and sentenced to imprisonment (unless pardoned or disability removed by Central Government); being a legal practitioner guilty of professional misconduct; being a chartered accountant guilty of negligence or misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of renewal fees to remain on register (Rule 115)
rubrics_metrics.description: For continuance of the name in the register a patent agent must pay the annual renewal fee specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example fee specified: Rs.500 per year in the First Schedule. Name is maintained by annual payment; failure can lead to deletion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alteration of names, addresses or qualifications in register (Rule 118)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent agent may apply for alteration of his name, principal place of business, branch offices or qualifications entered in the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On receipt of application and fee, the Controller will cause necessary alterations. Every alteration will be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of names of patent agents (Rule 120)
rubrics_metrics.description: Names and addresses of registered patent agents will be published from time to time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication channels include official journal, newspapers, trade journals, Annual Report of Controller General, and such other manner as Controller deems fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of practice as a patent agent
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered patent agent can practice before the Controller and, if duly authorized, sign applications and communications and perform specified acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice includes drafting specifications, making applications for patents, making subsequent correspondence with the Patent Office, attending hearings, filing/participating in opposition proceedings, defending against oppositions. Specifically: preparing specs/documents; applying for/obtaining patents in India or elsewhere; dealing with patent law of any country; giving advice other than scientific/technical as to validity or infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on corporate practice as patent agents (Section 129)
rubrics_metrics.description: No company or body corporate should practice or hold itself out as patent agents unless certain conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each person in the associate group, if any, must be a registered agent and duly authorized by the concerned person on whose behalf they act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal from register and grounds for removal (Section 130 and Rule 116)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Controller may remove a person's name from the register after opportunity to be heard and such inquiry as he thinks fit when satisfied of certain grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds include entry by error due to misrepresentation/suppression of material fact; conviction of an offence and sentence to imprisonment; misconduct in professional capacity rendering him unfit; default in payment of fees; death; request for removal. Removal is notified in Official Gazette and communicated to concerned person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration to register after removal (Rule 117)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Controller may, on application and sufficient cause shown, restore to the register the name of any person removed therefrom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application for restoration should be made in Form 2 within two months from date of removal (Rule 117(1)). Restoration will be notified in Official Gazette and communicated to the person. Name continues for one year from date on which last annual fee became due (Rule 117(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention of inventor as such in patent (Section 28 / Chapter XIV provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the inventor desires his name to be mentioned in a patent he may apply; Controller if satisfied will cause mention in complete specification and register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request period: 2 months after advertisement of acceptance of complete specification, extendable by one month. Requests before grant made on Form 8; claims by persons not the applicant must be accompanied by a statement setting out circumstances. Controller not entertain request if applicant wrongly obtained invention from actual inventor who could succeed in opposition under Section 25(1)(a). Oppositions handled per rules 58–63. If Controller allows, mention in prescribed form (rule 70) and register. Applications to remove or correct inventor mention follow same procedure with opportunity to be heard and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of patent granted to deceased applicant (Section 44)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Controller may amend the patent by substituting the name of the legal representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application in Form 10 with prescribed fee (Rs.1500 for natural person, Rs.6000 for legal entity) should be accompanied by evidence verifying statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of patent (Section 45)
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of patent is the date of filing of the application and is entered in the register of patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: calculate duration of patent and reckoning time for payment of renewal fee. Other provisions affecting date: antedating of complete specifications necessitated by division (section 16); post-dating by order of Controller for amendments to comply with office requirements (section 17); date of patent of addition determined by date of patent of main invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form, extent and effect of patent (Section 46)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent shall be in the prescribed form and shall have effect throughout India and shall be granted for one inventive concept only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent form is specified in the Third Schedule with modifications as circumstances require; patent bears the number accorded after grant of a complete specification which becomes the Patent number. Objection that patent was granted for more than one inventive concept is not competent in suit or other proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of Patentees (Section 48)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the subject matter is a product, the patentee has exclusive right to prevent third parties from making, using, offering for sale, selling or importing that product in India; for processes, right to prevent use of the process and products directly obtained by that process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rights are not infringed if the invention is used on foreign-registered vessels/aircraft or land vehicles owned by persons ordinarily resident in that foreign country when temporarily/accidentally in India; exceptions where foreign laws do not confer corresponding rights may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of co-owners of patents (Section 50)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent is granted to two or more persons, each is entitled to an equal undivided share unless an agreement provides otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each co-owner may enjoy rights for his own benefit without accounting to others, but license or assignment of their share requires consent of others. A purchaser from one co-owner can deal with the article as if sold by a sole patentee. Rules of law for ownership/devolution of movable property apply; provisions do not affect rights of trustees or legal representatives or assignees of partial interests created before the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of Controller to give directions to co-owners (Section 51)
rubrics_metrics.description: Controller may, on application by any registered grantee/proprietor, give directions as to sale/lease of patent interest, grant of licences, or exercise of any rights under section 50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications made in Form 11 with a statement of facts; copies sent to other grantees. If a registered person fails to execute instrument or do thing required within 14 days of written request, Controller may empower another person to execute in the defaulting person's name. Controller must give opportunity to be heard; directions shall not affect trustees/legal representatives or be inconsistent with agreements. Controller can grant a patent to the true and first inventor with same date/number as a patent revoked for fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of patent and renewal fees (Section 53 and Rule 80)
rubrics_metrics.description: Term of patent is 20 years from the date of the application for all patents, provided renewal fees are paid every year on due date or extended period (max six months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal fee payable at expiration of the second year from date of patent or of any succeeding year before expiration of the second or succeeding year. Annual fees for multiple years may be paid in advance; fees listed in First Schedule (entry no. 18). For patents granted later than two years from filing, fees that became due in the meantime may be paid within three months of recording or within the extended period not later than nine months from recording (Section 142(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent of addition: eligibility, term and validity (Sections 54–56)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent of addition covers a slight modification of an invention for which the applicant already has a patent and which does not involve a substantial inventive step; it cannot be granted before the main patent is granted and requires filing date same or later than main invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination whether proposed invention is an improvement/addition is based on comparison of novel contributions in each specification, not mere presence of common elements (case: Sadgrove v. Godfrey). Term runs concurrently with the main patent; if main patent revoked, patent of addition may become independent for remainder of term if ordered. No renewal fee payable for patent of addition while main patent remains in force; if it becomes independent, normal renewal fees apply. Validity of patent of addition cannot be questioned solely on ground it ought to have been subject of independent patent or that it lacks inventive step relative to main invention. For novelty, the complete specification of main invention may be cited as anticipatory publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of lapsed patents (Section 60) — conditions for restoration
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent has ceased to have effect because of non-payment of renewal fees, it may be restored provided application is made without undue delay and within 18 months from date of cessation, and failure to pay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must be on Form 15 with supporting evidence; any patent of addition to be restored should be specified (separate Form 15 for each main patent; no fee for patent of addition). Applicant must be patentee or legal representative; assignee may apply only when assignment is registered. If patentee failed to register change of name before cessation, must first correct register; identity proof required if name changed after cessation. The application must include a statement fully setting out circumstances leading to non-payment supported by recent evidence; evidence may cover several patents and must support claim of unintentional failure and no undue delay. Controller may call further evidence. Deliberate election not to pay fee under erroneous supposition is fatal; financial inconvenience is not ground (destitution may be considered). Negligence of agent may be sufficient if proved. If no prima facie case, applicant notified and may be refused unless requests hearing within one month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to restoration (Section 61 grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person interested may oppose restoration within two months of the advertisement in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds of opposition: (a) failure to pay the renewal fee was not unintentional; and/or (b) there has been undue delay in making the application.
